title: Earth Is Lumpy as Hell
author: Jake Currie
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementGeoscienceEarth Is Lumpy as HellIt’s what’s on the inside that countsJCBy Jake Currie8:30 AM CDT on July 30, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleAs the crew of Apollo 17 zoomed toward the moon, they looked back and snapped a photo of home. That image, the famed “Blue Marble” photo, shows Earth from the South Pole to the Mediterranean Sea, in all its spherical glory. Now NASA has released a new image of our planet, and let’s just say it’s not as aesthetically pleasing. Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoLUMPY BLUE DOT: The Geoid, with the geoid height exaggerated by a factor of 10,000. Credit: Scott Luthcke/Mark SubbaRao/NASA/GSFC.If you’re thinking to yourself, “that’s not what Earth looks like!!!” you’re right (so calm down). It’s not a photo, it’s an image of what Earth’s gravitational field looks like, compiled from more than a billion observations from 19 satellites (and exaggerated by a factor of 10,000 for effect). If you were somehow able to fill all the fissures and trenches with spackle and sand down the mountains, this is the (again, exaggerated) shape the ocean would take. Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
